checks.reason: For nonnegative nonzero z in C_c^inf, U_z=Gamma*z is globally bounded by local Radon mass, hence lambda_z(c)^2=sup_g(c*int U_z g^2 - b(g)) is finite with Lambda(c)<=c*||U_z||_inf. Positivity for every c>0 has the c>0-free gain/kinetic comparison (c*C_Gamma*L^{-alpha} - D*L^{-2}>0 since alpha<2), supplied by 129/118. Supremum of affine functions with slopes in [0, ||U_z||_inf] gives |Lambda(c)-Lambda(d)|<=||U_z||_inf*|c-d|, and on positive compact [c-,c+] the floor Lambda(c-)>=lambda_z(c-)^2>0 gives |lambda_z(c)-lambda_z(d)|<=||U_z||_inf*|c-d|/(2*lambda_z(c-)). The cutoff f_n=f_a*chi(1/(nt))*chi(1/(n(1-t))) is smooth compact after zero extension, nonzero near 1/2, increasing in n, f_n<=f_a, and f_n↑f_a pointwise. Thus k_n(s)=int|s-t|^{-a}f_n(t)dt↑int|s-t|^{-a}f_a(t)dt=1 at every s in [0,1] by MCT and PROOF134; with c0=int f_4>0 (f_4=f_a on [1/4,3/4]) and kernel |s-t|^{-a}>=1 off the diagonal, c0<=k_n(s)<=1. The mean of Psi_n=f_n (x) z is k_n(s)U_z, so its unique Rayleigh rate is lambda_z(k_n(s)), bounded by lambda_z(1) and converging pointwise; DCT gives I_{Psi_n}->lambda_z(1). The score limit is valid without monotonicity of the differences because both component limits exist separately.

For smooth compact unit real g, b(g)=||nabla g||_2^2>0 because zero weak gradient forces the Fourier transform to be supported on the null singleton {0}, hence g=0. A=A_sp(g)=B_Gamma(g^2,g^2) is finite (compact support) and positive by the continuous autocorrelation C_{g^2}(0)=||g||_4^4>0 plus Gamma(B_rho)>0. For U_ell g(x)=ell^{d/2}g(ell x): b(U_ell g)=ell^2 b, and A_sp(U_ell g)=ell^alpha A from factors ell^{2d} (two squares), ell^{-d} (dx), ell^{alpha-d} (Radon pushforward of Gamma). With z=theta(U_ell g)^2, testing with U_ell g gives lambda_z(1)^2>=theta*ell^alpha*A - ell^2*b and B_Gamma(z,z)=theta^2*ell^alpha*A. The choices ell^2=u L^2/b and theta=(1+u)L^2/(ell^alpha A) make the radicand exactly theta*ell^alpha*A-ell^2*b=(1+u)L^2-u L^2=L^2, so S1pos>=L-C(u)L^q with C(u)=M_a(1+u)^2/(2 R u^{alpha/2}). The logarithmic derivative is 2/(1+u)-alpha/(2u)=(q u-alpha)/(2u(1+u)), so u*=alpha/q is the global minimum; 1+u*=4/q. Then max_{L>0}(L-CL^q) at L*=(qC)^{-1/k} equals (k/q)(qC)^{-1/k}=k[q^q C]^{-1/k}. Substituting u* gives q^q C = 8 M_a q^{q/2}/(R alpha^{alpha/2}), since q+alpha/2-2=q/2 under q=4-alpha; this matches the stated denominator 8. Inverting the inequality bounds each R(g) by a finite number, and a normalized compact bump gives A,b>0, so 0<R0<infinity.

Semantic join PROOF134->PROOF136 closes. With r=(1-a)/2 one has -a=2r-1. For 0<s<1 the left potential L(s) equals r*Beta(1-r,2r)*B_s(r,r), and reflection plus B_s+B_{1-s}=Beta(r,r) give the full unnormalized value r*Beta(1-r,2r)*Beta(r,r)=Gamma(r)Gamma(1-r)=D_r. At s=0 the direct integral is int t^{r-1}(1-t)^{-r}dt=Beta(r,1-r)=D_r; s=1 follows by reflection, so the endpoints are direct computations and not unjustified limits. The mass is M_a=Beta(1-r,1-r)/D_r=Gamma(1-r)/(Gamma(2-2r)Gamma(r))=Gamma((1+a)/2)/(Gamma(1+a)Gamma((1-a)/2)), unchanged and generally not one. The n=4 cutoff is exactly f_a on [1/4,3/4], so c0>=int_{1/4}^{3/4}f_a>0; the zero neighborhoods are t<=1/(2n) and t>=1-1/(2n), so zero extension is C_c^inf. The c-floor c0>0 is needed because sqrt(c) at c=n^{-2} has difference quotient n from zero; the construction stays in [c0,1] with Lambda(c0)>0.

Semantic join 117/135->136 closes. PROOF117 gives v_{Psi_n}=E[W(Psi_n)^2]=int Psi_n(s,x) h_s(x) ds dx exactly. For Psi_n=f_n (x) z this equals B_Gamma(z,z)*int_0^1 int_0^1 f_n(s)f_n(t)|s-t|^{-a} ds dt = B_Gamma(z,z)*int_0^1 f_n(s)k_n(s) ds; Tonelli is valid for nonnegative integrands with alpha0<1, and the symmetric double integral needs no extra factor 2 or 1/2. B_Gamma(z,z) is finite (<=||z||_2^2 Gamma(K-K)) and positive: C_z(y)=int z(x)z(x-y)dx is continuous with C_z(0)=||z||_2^2>0, so on some B_rho it exceeds ||z||_2^2/2, while homogeneity gives Gamma(B_rho)=rho^{d-alpha}Gamma(B_1)>0 by exhaustion of the nonzero measure from origin-centered balls. The product f_n(s)k_n(s) increases to f_a(s) at a.e. interior s, so v_{Psi_n}→M_a B_Gamma(z,z)=(M_a/2)B_Gamma(z,z) after the half action; only the origin ball and the given W are used, not translated-ball positivity or an unmasked eigenstate.

Semantic join 127/128/129/118->136 closes. Input128 bounds every h_s globally in space, so the original unmasked Gamma convolution U_z=Gamma*z is globally bounded and nonnegative. Input129 yields the real H^1 Rayleigh identity lambda_{Psi,s}^2=sup_{f in H^1(R^d;R), ||f||_2=1}(int h_s f^2 - ||nabla f||_2^2) with self-adjoint bottom; no unmasked ground eigenstate is asserted. Semantic join 136->137 closes. U_ell is unit-L2 preserving; b(U_ell g)=ell^2 b by Lebesgue substitution, while A_sp(U_ell g)=ell^alpha A combines ell^{2d}, ell^{-d}, and the homogeneous Radon pushforward ell^{alpha-d}; this distingishes the Radon factor from Lebesgue volume and covers singular/white covariances. The test z=theta(U_ell g)^2 is nonnegative smooth compact, so the 136 inequality applies and the Rayleigh trial gives only a lower bound lambda_z(1)^2>=theta*ell^alpha*A-ell^2*b (never equality). Under ell^2=u L^2/b and theta=(1+u)L^2/(ell^alpha A), the radicand is L^2 and the half cost is C(u)L^q. At u=alpha/q the coefficient C is minimized, 1+u=4/q, and q^q C=8 M_a q^{q/2}/(R alpha^{alpha/2}); the scalar maximum k[q^q C]^{-1/k} reproduces the asserted constant with the factor 8 from the half action together with (1+u*)^2=16/q^2. All exponents were independently checked for the white alpha=1 and d^3 alpha=3/2, a=1/4 cases.
